formattedAddress: No. 20號, Lane 505, Section 5, Zhongshan N Rd, Fulin Village, Shilin District, Taipei City, Taiwan 111

text.text: Very good pasta with tasty Korean sauce, I also like their appetizers (Korean fried chicken, seafood pancake and soup).  It’s a creative Korean Italian fusion.

text.text: As a California girl that has been living in Taipei for almost 4 years, I can confidently say this place is above and beyond most of the competition. The textures and flavors are artfully combined, expertly prepared and present a really beautiful fusion of Korean and Italian style cuisine. This isn't just a pasta shop, which many places in the area will do an "ok" job at - the ingredients are fresh, and present crunchy, chewy, tender, spicy and umami in symphony. I've been here a handful of times and am consistently impressed.

Love the seafood pancakes - crispy and packed with ingredients. Can taste the seafood in every bite. Will try the pasta next time as those are the specialty.
Burger patty is tasty but the sauce is a bit too sweet to my likings.

text.text:
Sure the food was not terrible but I don't get the hype.. We got the beef ball and chicken pasta, both were mediocre. The chicken pasta's sauce was bland and a bit on the watery side for pasta sauce in my opinion and the beef's one was basically gochujang, pretty boring and unnecessarily overpowering. I don't understand the tiny pieces of veggies either, pretty uncommon on a pasta dish (we ended up eating with a spoon since it was not very practical to eat with a fork).
For appetizer we got the seaweed roll, which was very disappointing since the tempura batter was hard, not crispy as expected.
I guess the highlight of the meal was the cantaloupe soda, which was from a can (also unexpected).
To sum up, the experience felt almost like self-service. We ordered by checking off dishes on a paper menu, and we also helped ourselves to free water and napkins at a station. Additionally, we arrived before the restaurant's opening hour (5:30 p.m.), and waited outside with a few other groups. However, when it was 5:30, the staff remained inside, chatting, and we weren’t sure when it was okay to enter. It wasn’t until a delivery person arrived that my husband followed him in and asked the staff if we could come in. Only then did we realize that we could. Despite having a glass door, which allowed the staff to see us waiting outside, no one made an effort to welcome us in when it was finally time for the restaurant to open.
